overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford Family Network leaders Marie Cassidy and Irina Shumway about the organization's 33-year history of community service and its comprehensive support programs for local families. The discussion focused on the network's current funding crisis following the loss of a major grant and provided information on how citizens can assist with sustainability efforts.

items.title: Show Introduction and Guest Backgrounds
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Marie Cassidy and Irina Shumway, who discussed their extensive backgrounds in social work and their personal motivations for serving Medford families.

items.title: History and Founding of the Medford Family Network
items.summary: Marie Cassidy recounted founding the Medford Family Network (MFN) in 1993 following a grant initiative, while Irina Shumway shared her experience transitioning from a parent participant to a leadership role.

items.title: Overview of Comprehensive Family Services
items.summary: Guests detailed MFN's free services for families with children aged birth to eight, including curriculum-based playgroups, school readiness programs, and monthly distributions of diapers and toiletries.

items.title: Program Successes and Funding Challenges
items.summary: The speakers highlighted MFN's high referral volume and cultural impact before disclosing that a primary grant representing half of their budget will end on July 1st. Cassidy stated that the organization is now seeking new support from the city and school department to sustain operations.

items.title: Fundraising and Community Donation Opportunities
items.summary: Discussion focused on the fundraising efforts of the Friends of the Medford Family Network and how citizens can provide monetary donations, volunteer for event planning, or donate goods to the 'freebie foyer.'

items.title: City and Institutional Partnerships
items.summary: Cassidy described collaborations with the Medford Housing Authority, the Office of Prevention and Outreach, and Medford High School's vocational departments to provide multilingual support and specialized services.

items.title: 33rd Anniversary and Summer Event Preview
items.summary: The guests concluded by announcing upcoming summer events, including a dance-a-thon, the annual Teddy Bear Picnic, and several outdoor concerts. The interview ended with a call for organizational sustainability and continued community engagement.
